lead.headline: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet, so agents can pay without ever seeing your card
lead.summary: Built with American Express, Mastercard and Visa, the wallet lets you add a card once and then approve each agent purchase with a security check such as Face ID or a fingerprint, after reviewing the items, total and card. The payment network hands out a token in place of the real card details, and existing rewards and dispute protections still apply. It starts with ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US, through dots, alongside tools and guidance for businesses that want to accept agent payments.

number_of_day.label: LangSmith customers LangChain now claims, as it raises $300M at a $3B valuation, more than double its value a year ago.

news.headline: LangChain raises a $300M Series C at a $3B valuation
news.summary: CapitalG led the round, with GIC, DFJ Growth, IVP and Sapphire Ventures joining. The open-source library from 2022 has turned into an agent-management business: LangSmith pitches itself as model- and cloud-neutral, with customers such as Harvey, Rippling, Clay, Nvidia, Toyota and Salesforce.

news.headline: OpenAI disbands its stand-alone robotics team
news.summary: Robotics researchers move into the main research org under Mark Chen, and applied robotics and hardware staff into Applied under Greg Brockman. OpenAI says it is betting on general-purpose models driving robots directly, not retreating. Its booth at the CoRL robotics conference in Austin this week sat empty.

news.headline: Perplexity brings Teammates, its always-on agents, to the Mac
news.summary: Teammates are given an ongoing responsibility, such as triaging bug reports, tracking metrics or running a growth campaign, then plan the work, bring in more agents as it grows and report back for review. Previously on iOS and the web, it needs a Perplexity Max subscription.

news.headline: Peter Sarlin's PostScriptum takes a majority stake in Finnish AI consultancy Brillian
news.summary: Founded in 2024, Brillian does AI deployment end to end, from strategy to everyday use, from two Finnish hubs, and earns most of its revenue abroad with clients such as Siemens, Storytel and Carnival Cruise Lines. The founders and staff keep a substantial minority, and the plan is bigger projects and new AI hubs next year.
